title: How many components, and can they be moved separately?
question: Is pain one experience or separable parts (how strong vs how bad), and can one part be changed without the other?
status_reason: Same asymmetry read as seriality (price2000) or near-unitary (talbot2019); 2023-24 studies call it graded; no E1-E2 primary study moves intensity alone.
status_scope: Talbot's review covered cognitive manipulations only; drug and lesion evidence enters through a few small separate studies.

title: What is the non-sensory component: evaluation, command, or something else?
question: What makes pain (and other feelings) bad: a perception of badness, a command, a desire, or something else?
status_reason: Latest exchange (mb2026 reply to carruthers2023) has no counter-reply in the corpus; imperativists also split among themselves (kauppinen2021 vs bh2019).
status_scope: Seed survey favoured imperativism: imperativist authors wrote 14 reviewed works, evaluativists 7; several evaluativist replies are not held.

title: Why take painkillers? The direction of pain's motivation
question: Does unpleasantness itself push us to get rid of the feeling, or only to protect the body, with relief-seeking coming from elsewhere?
status_reason: Four rival accounts persist (martinez2015, bain2019, loopy2019, kauppinen2021) and carruthers2023 presses a hedonism charge; no side concedes in the corpus.
status_scope: Replies directly on this question (Cutter & Tye 2014, Jacobson 2019) are not held.

title: Is asymbolic pain pain, and what does it show?
question: When patients say a pinprick hurts but do not mind it, are they in pain, and does this show pain has separable parts?
status_reason: No clinical evidence newer than 1999 enters the record; the active 2023-25 exchange moves only by reinterpretation of old case reports.
status_scope: Case reports are known only second-hand; Grahek 2007 and Bain 2014, central to the exchange, are not held.

title: Is felt unpleasantness separable from avoidance and motivation?
question: Is how bad pain feels the same thing as the push to avoid or escape it, or can the two be measured and moved apart?
status_reason: Behaviour moved without ratings (claes2015, flury2025) but across phases or probe trials; no reviewed study rates own unpleasantness and avoidance per trial.
status_scope: Placebo and desire-for-relief work that rated desire beside pain is largely outside the corpus (vase2003, vase2005 named-only).

title: Where does pain meet action in cortex?
question: Is cingulate activity during pain about feeling bad, about general control, or about preparing an action?
status_reason: Integration (shackman2011) and action-dependence (perini2013, koppel2022) readings coexist unadjudicated; the one lesion study did not measure pain.
status_scope: The action-dependence line is mostly one lab's studies; counter-evidence such as Kragel 2018 is cited but not held.

title: Is pain's felt badness the learning signal, and how is learning from pain structured?
question: Nociceptive input supports aversive learning; is pain's felt badness itself that teaching signal, and do people learn more from pain received or avoided?
status_reason: Identity claims (seymour2019; johansen2004 one-circuit) are untested against felt badness; learning asymmetry conflicts (jepma2022 vs le2024).
status_scope: The reviewed computational papers were selected for this framing; that nociceptive input drives aversive learning is treated as uncontested background.

title: What drives pain-related avoidance and disability?
question: Do people avoid painful activity because of fear, because of pain itself, or because avoiding pain wins out over other goals?
status_reason: The originators' 2016 model keeps the fear loop and adds a goal-priority fork (crombez2012, vlaeyen2016); causal tests remain few (leeuw2006, claes2015).
status_scope: Only the fear-avoidance originators' programme is reviewed; rival clinical models (e.g. endurance responses, hasenbring2010) are named-only.
